dimensions.reasons: The submitted scene clearly depicts a retro-industrial letter-assembly machine: Group A wide views show a bench-mounted conveyor, exposed gear-and-rod mechanism, and two overhead manipulators, while Group B progresses from a single M in momentum_0041 to the completed gold word in momentum_0200. However, the machine reads more as a simplified display rig than the layered, clearly teachable mechanical linkage requested.
issues: The robotic pick-and-place system is not convincingly realized as two three-joint arms.
The linkage chain between gears, cams, rods, conveyor, and arms is visually unclear.
All Group C video samples show essentially the same early M-plus-motion-blurred-O composition, with no visible progression despite the Group B image sequence showing assembly.

dimensions.reasons: The bench, conveyor bed, railings, gear panel, and camshaft assembly are substantially built and supported. In contrast, Group A wide_front, wide_back, and the isometric views clearly show the right bent arm floating above the conveyor without a base, rail, or visible articulated mount; the left arm's connection is also ambiguous.
issues: The right-hand manipulator is unsupported and floats above the work surface.
The left manipulator reads as a partially connected lever rather than an articulated arm with anchored joints.
The airborne O in Group C has no visible gripper or support, so the intended pick-and-place action is physically unconvincing.

dimensions.reasons: The gold extruded MOMENTUM letters are bold, legible, beveled-looking sans-serif forms, and the toothed gear silhouettes, conveyor slats, shafts, rails, and rivets read clearly as industrial components. Group B momentum_0200 gives a strong metallic-gold title result.
issues: The arm silhouettes read as thick dark angular levers rather than recognizable three-joint robots.
Brass surfaces are predominantly clean and glossy rather than visibly worn or lightly oxidized.
Much of the steel framework is pale white/gray and visually generic instead of convincingly cool clear-coated steel.

dimensions.reasons: The designated author renders in Group B are cleanly rendered with coherent depth of field, plausible shadows, reflective metal, and a workshop-like blurred setting. The final title frame, momentum_0200, is visually polished enough to read as a stylized 3D title sequence.
issues: The strongly blurred workshop background and bright circular lamp reduce environmental credibility and obscure the setting.
The simplified, floating arm elements break the illusion of a functioning physical machine.
Materials and construction lack the irregular wear, oxidation, and dense mechanical detail expected of an old industrial apparatus.

dimensions.reasons: The main spatial organization is sensible: Group A places the gear/cam panel at one end of the long bench, the conveyor centrally along it, and two intended manipulators above the belt. Group B positions the completed letters in a single readable row across the front of the mechanism.
issues: The arms are spatially separated from the drive hardware, so their supposed mechanical relationship to the cams and rods is not clear.
The large final letters substantially occlude the conveyor and mechanism in momentum_0120 through momentum_0200, reducing the requested layer-by-layer teaching clarity.
No distinct title-card structure is evident behind or around the locked final word.

dimensions.reasons: The relative scale of the long workbench, belt, prominent main gear, smaller driven gears, and large display letters is generally coherent. The completed word nearly spans the length of the assembly in Group B momentum_0200, which gives the scene a plausible kinetic-typography scale.
issues: The suspended arm pieces appear underspecified and disproportionate relative to the large letter forms they are meant to manipulate.
The shallow, layered rail construction looks more like decorative fascia than a robust conveyor/assembly system.

dimensions.reasons: Group B uses warm workshop illumination, a cooler blue-toned background influence, clear specular highlights on the gold type and brass gears, and reasonably soft shadows. The metal title has attractive reflective definition in momentum_0120 and momentum_0200, while the tabletop remains comparatively matte.
issues: The brass lacks convincing oxidation, grime, and worn variation.
The bright white/cream steel rails and frame do not consistently read as cool gray clear-coated steel.
The shallow depth of field makes parts of the workshop and some machine detail needlessly indistinct for an instructional mechanical demonstration.

dimensions.reasons: Visible required elements include a bench, rails and rivets, a long conveyor-like belt, a multi-size gear cluster, cam/rod components, two intended overhead manipulators, and all eight letters of MOMENTUM in Group B momentum_0200. The Group B export images also visibly show staged accumulation of the letters.
issues: The required pair of camshafts driving clearly identifiable reciprocating push rods is not independently clear; Group A detail_gear_cams mainly reveals one prominent shaft with several discs.
The two required three-joint robotic arms are not convincingly present as complete, supported robotic assemblies.
Scattered letter blanks and a dedicated locked title-card finish are not clearly shown.
The supplied Group C animation frames do not visibly demonstrate the complete assembly sequence or camera orbit.

criteria.criterion: The complete machine choreography must assemble and lock MOMENTUM through a synchronized, unobstructed, pedagogically readable sequence.
The complete gear train must satisfy the stated dimensions, common-module compatibility, connected engagement, and mechanically compatible operation.
Two identifiable camshafts must each produce recurring push-rod reciprocation.
The conveyor must have the stated transport length and visibly feed letter blanks into the handling workflow.
Two three-joint robotic arms must both perform letter pick-and-place.
All eight title letters must share the specified bold sans-serif form and dimensions.
The supporting bench must satisfy its dimensions, base role, construction detailing, and complete dark matte wood finish.
The machine must achieve the requested retro-industrial kinetic-typography identity through a coherent old mechanism and its complete brass-and-steel surface system.
criteria.evidence: The exported frames show recognizable gold/brass-colored gears and glossy gold typography alongside pale grey structural parts, but the brass surfaces appear uniformly clean and polished rather than visibly worn or lightly oxidized. The grey/white components do not consistently read as a distinct cool-grey clear-coated steel material, so the complete requested brass-and-steel surface system is not demonstrated.

criteria.criterion: The native lighting setup and authored result must jointly provide the requested warm key, cool rim, ambient fill, and interior HDRI.
The authored shot must use the requested ordered movement, focal length, and readable shallow-focus treatment.
The delivered Blender project must be openable, editable, complete, and preserve the requested native Cycles rendering configuration and motion-blur result.
The actual PNG sequence and composited MP4 must form a complete, openable output package with the required resolution and timing.

notes: The submission successfully establishes a recognizable industrial conveyor-and-gear typography machine and visibly reaches a legible MOMENTUM title in the Group B render sequence. Its main weaknesses are the unsupported, overly abstract arm mechanisms, unclear drive-chain connections, clean generic materials, and conflicting Group C video evidence that shows no visible progression across the sampled animation.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
